questiontext.text: In a threaded binary tree, what do the threads reuse or replace?

feedback.text: Correct — pointers that would be NULL are repurposed as threads.
No — the payload is untouched; only unused child pointers become threads.

answer.text: The real links to existing children

feedback.text: No — genuine child links are kept; only NULL links become threads.

answer.text: The root pointer of the tree

feedback.text: No — threading concerns the leaf-level NULL child pointers, not the root handle.

generalfeedback.text: Threading fills the wasted, otherwise-NULL child pointers with useful links (threads) instead of leaving them empty.

questiontext.text: A thread points to a node's ______ in the traversal order.

feedback.text: Correct — a left thread points to the in-order predecessor, a right thread to the in-order successor.
No — threads follow the in-order sequence, not level-order.
No — a thread targets the in-order neighbor, which is not necessarily the parent.
No — threads point to adjacent nodes in in-order sequence.

generalfeedback.text: A right thread links to the in-order successor and a left thread to the in-order predecessor, so you can walk the tree in in-order without recursion.

questiontext.text: What is the main benefit of a threaded binary tree?

answer.text: In-order traversal without recursion or an explicit stack, in O(1) extra space

feedback.text: Correct — threads let you find the next node directly.

answer.text: It makes search O(1) in the worst case

feedback.text: No — search cost is unchanged by threading.

answer.text: It removes the need to store any data in nodes

feedback.text: No — data is still stored; only NULL pointers are reused.
No — threading does not change the tree's shape or balance.

generalfeedback.text: Because each thread points at the in-order successor/predecessor, you can traverse in-order iteratively using O(1) extra space.

questiontext.text: How does the structure tell a real child link apart from a thread?

answer.text: A boolean flag per pointer marks it as a child link or a thread

feedback.text: Correct — each node stores a tag bit for its left and right pointers.
No — a thread is a non-NULL link; that is the whole point.

answer.text: By comparing the pointer's numeric address to the root

feedback.text: No — a per-pointer flag is what marks the difference, not address arithmetic.

answer.text: Real children are stored in a separate array

feedback.text: No — both kinds share the same pointer field, distinguished by a flag.

generalfeedback.text: Each pointer carries a tag (e.g. isThread) so traversal knows whether to descend into a child or follow a thread.

questiontext.text: A threaded binary tree enables in-order traversal without recursion or an explicit stack.

feedback.text: Correct — threads provide the next in-order node directly, using O(1) extra space.
It does — that is the primary purpose of threading.

questiontext.text: In a threaded binary tree, a thread points to the node's level-order successor.

feedback.text: No — threads follow the in-order sequence, not level-order.
Correct — a thread points to the in-order predecessor or successor.

questiontext.text: The special link that replaces an otherwise-NULL child pointer and points to an in-order neighbor is called a ______.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
Correct.

questiontext.text: Which statements about threaded binary trees are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: Threads reuse pointers that would otherwise be NULL

feedback.text: Yes — wasted NULL child pointers become threads.

answer.text: A boolean flag distinguishes a thread from a real child link

feedback.text: Yes — each pointer carries a tag bit.

answer.text: Threading requires an auxiliary stack proportional to tree height

feedback.text: No — the point of threading is O(1) extra space with no stack.

answer.text: Threads point to a node's level-order successor

feedback.text: No — threads point to in-order predecessor/successor.

generalfeedback.text: Threads fill NULL child pointers, are marked by a flag, target in-order neighbors, and permit stackless in-order traversal in O(1) space.
